subject: Intermittent chat response elongation — customer notification & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@acme.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: support@acme.co
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Notice: chat responses becoming elongated (long pauses mid-response)

Hi Ben,

Over the last hour our production chat widgets have started returning long pauses mid-response — the assistant will stream a handful of tokens and then sit quiet for 4-8 seconds before continuing. This is impacting user experience; throughput is fine but perceived latency is spiking.

We captured a few session IDs and attached a sample session export (acme-sample-session.json). Can you confirm whether this is on your side, and if there are any immediate mitigations we can apply while you investigate?

Session IDs: acme-prod-1, acme-prod-7
Environment: us-east-1 region, model: rw-open-13b, streaming enabled with chunk_size=256

Thanks,
Elena Vargas
Senior Product Manager, Acme Co
elena.vargas@acme.co

Attachments: acme-sample-session.json
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@acme.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:02:18 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: chat responses becoming elongated (long pauses mid-response)

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up and the session export. We’re seeing correlated traces from our edge layer that line up with the timestamps you included. Short answer: not a client-side bug.

Immediate actions we recommend while we triage:
- Switch the affected clients to non-streaming (polling) fallback for short windows (this avoids the streaming buffer behavior).
- Reduce the streaming chunk_size to 64 or 128 tokens (you can change in the SDK by setting stream_chunk_size).
- Enable client-side keepalive pings (every 10s) to maintain socket activity — this prevents some proxy timeouts showing as pauses.

We’ve opened ticket INF-3456 and engineering is collecting telemetry. Attaching a short diagnostic snapshot we pulled: rdw-diag-snapshot-0620.txt.

I’ll have Marissa take the lead on root cause and a targeted mitigation we can ship today. Grace, assigning to you for priority if we need a Dedicated pool switch.

Next step: I’ll share a short advisory you can paste into your status channel once we confirm the mitigation window.

– Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachments: rdw-diag-snapshot-0620.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@acme.co>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 14:30:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: chat responses becoming elongated (long pauses mid-response)

Thanks for the data, Elena — we dug in and have a short hypothesis and mitigation.

What we observed (summary):
- A subset of requests hitting the streaming path were being migrated between edge workers after the first token stream, causing the server-side KV cache to be re-warmed and producing 3–9s gaps in token emission.
- The migration is correlated with an autoscaling/placement jitter introduced by a recent scheduler tweak that affected a small percentage of pods in us-east-1.

Short-term mitigations we’re pushing now (applied at 14:15 UTC):
1) Sticky routing for active streaming sessions for 60s (prevents mid-stream worker handoffs).
2) Lowering the default stream_chunk_size to 96 for affected tenant routes (reduces large token batches and reduces chance of preemption).
3) Rolling a targeted scheduler rollback on the small edge pool (will complete in ~40m).

Client-side changes we recommend (if you can deploy quickly):
- Implement a small socket-level heartbeat (10s) and treat pause >2s as recoverable (show typing indicator) rather than abandoning the stream.
- If you need an immediate UX fix, switch to short non-streaming responses for flows where uninterrupted token flow matters (e.g., form autofill).

We’re continuing to monitor. I’ll post updates to the INF-3456 ticket and the Acme incident notes (link below).

Marissa Cole
SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3456
Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vargas <elena.vargas@acme.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 15:43:11 -07:00
Subject: Status update: elongated streaming responses — mitigation applied & next steps

Hi Elena — quick update following up on yesterday’s activity.

What we completed:
- Rolled back the scheduler tweak on the affected edge pool (completed 2028-06-20 15:05 UTC).
- Enabled sticky routing for active streaming sessions for 60s across the us-east-1 path.
- Deployed a conservative stream_chunk_size default for tenant routes experiencing elevated pauses.

Impact observed:
- We’ve seen a reduction in mid-response pauses from ~6s median to ~0.6s median across the sample windows for Acme’s traffic over the past 24 hours.
- No measurable throughput decrease; token-cost impact is negligible.

Recommended next steps for Acme (action owners included):
- Elena/Product: Consider shipping an SDK config change to lower stream_chunk_size to 128 for chat flows sensitive to pauses (ETA: your next deploy).
- Acme Eng: Add a 10s keepalive heartbeat in the widget (short patch, low risk).
- Ben: I’ll coordinate a short postmortem summary and share a customer-facing advisory you can include in your incident timeline.
- Marissa/Grace: Evaluate whether a longer-term scheduler guard is needed to prevent future placement jitter.

We’ll leave INF-3456 open until you confirm a stable baseline for 48 hours; I’ll also share the postmortem doc and the customer advisory in Drive.

If you want immediate rollback to an isolated Dedicated pool for the most critical flows, Grace can scope cost/lead time.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — please reply here once you’ve validated the UX improvements on your side.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachments: acme-final-sample-afterfix.json (summary of sample session after mitigations)
